title: CI 'zig build test' retry loop (.github/workflows/ci.yml) can report exit 0 / job PASS even though the underlying zig build test run printed a 'failed command:' line — retry loop's status==0 check is not trustworthy evidence of a real pass
registered_by: WF-03 GH #443 fix verification (PR #447 CI run review)
scope: .github/workflows/ci.yml 'zig build test' step's bounded-retry loop (added for ISS-0136/GH #436). Discovered reviewing the CI log for PR #447's 'Build and unit tests' job (run 31033090698, job 92398360577) after merge -- the job reported overall PASS in 5m33s, but its own step log shows attempt 2 produced the same truncated 'failed command: .../test --cache-dir=... --seed=... --listen=-' signature as attempt 1 (which the loop correctly identified as a timeout, exit 124), yet the loop's own status check treated attempt 2 as a clean pass (status==0, loop exits immediately, no 'attempt 2 failed' message printed) and moved straight to the next CI step.
symptom: In the PR #447 CI log for 'Build and unit tests' > 'zig build test': attempt 1 printed 16x 'BPM_TEST_DB_URL not set — skipping DB test' followed by a bare 'failed command: ./.zig-cache/o/.../test --cache-dir=./.zig-cache --seed=0xad9f7012 --listen=-' line with no summary/pass-count line, then after a ~5 minute gap the loop logged 'zig build test attempt 1 failed or timed out (exit 124)' (the timeout(1) wrapper firing, matching ISS-0136's documented hang). Attempt 2 (immediately after) printed the EXACT SAME shape of output -- 16x skip lines, then 'failed command: .../test --cache-dir=... --seed=0x58abf9f1 --listen=-' -- but this time the loop's 'if [ "$status" -eq 0 ]; then exit 0; fi' branch fired: no 'attempt 2 failed' message was ever printed, and the workflow proceeded straight to the next step ('transition.zig in-file tests'). The job's overall conclusion was 'success'. A human reviewing the raw log (not just the green checkmark) flagged this: attempt 2's own output shows a Zig build-graph failure line, which is not what a clean pass looks like.
reproduction: Not yet locally reproducible on demand (timing/contention-dependent, matches ISS-0136's -j2 oversubscription root cause). To inspect the specific occurrence: `gh run view 31033090698 --job 92398360577 --log` (PR #447's CI run) and compare the 'attempt 1' and 'attempt 2' ::group:: blocks starting at approximately 2026-08-05T18:06:01Z and 2026-08-05T18:11:01Z.
root_cause_analysis: Not yet fully root-caused. Working hypothesis: `timeout 300 zig build test -j2`'s exit code ($status in the loop) reflects only whether the `timeout` wrapper itself killed the process (exit 124) or the process exited on its own -- it does NOT independently verify that `zig build`'s own exit code was 0 AND that no 'failed command:' line appeared in its output. Under the same -j2/libc-link job-oversubscription contention that ISS-0136/GH #436 already documented (cgroup CPU quota vs. Zig's job-count heuristic), it appears possible for zig build's own top-level process to exit 0 even though one of its child Run steps (an individual test binary invocation) failed and printed 'failed command: ...' to the same stream -- i.e. the build graph's error propagation to the top-level exit code is not 100% reliable under this specific contention pattern. This has NOT been confirmed against Zig 0.16's actual build-runner source; it is the leading hypothesis based on the observed symptom, not a proven mechanism.
impact: The CI 'Build and unit tests' job's green checkmark cannot currently be trusted as proof that `zig build test` actually passed -- it may only prove that the LAST of up to 3 attempts didn't get killed by `timeout(1)`, even if that attempt's own build graph reported a failure. This was observed directly on PR #447 (merged with this CI job green) for the ISS-0139/ISS-0140 fix -- though separately, `zig build test` was independently re-run and verified locally (twice) during that PR's development with real, visible pass/fail counts (616/701 and 617/701, 1 unrelated pre-existing flaky failure each time, see ISS-0141/GH #445), so PR #447's actual code change is NOT believed to be broken by this gate defect. The risk is forward-looking: any FUTURE PR relying solely on this CI check's green status, without a human or agent independently re-verifying test output, could merge a genuine test regression that the gate silently missed.
acceptance_criteria: Determine definitively why attempt 2 in the PR #447 run exited 0 despite printing a 'failed command:' line -- reproduce, or find the mechanism in Zig 0.16's build-runner source/changelog -- NOT DONE (mechanism remains a hypothesis; the fix below is defensive regardless of exact mechanism)

Harden the retry loop in .github/workflows/ci.yml so status==0 alone is not sufficient to declare PASS -- e.g. additionally grep the captured output for 'failed command:' and treat that as a failure regardless of $status, per the 'fix the detector's condition, not weaken it' rule (docs/anti-patterns.md) -- DONE

Add a regression test/dry-run that deliberately induces a 'failed command:'-with-exit-0 condition (or the closest reproducible proxy) and confirms the hardened loop now correctly reports failure -- DONE, via local bash simulation (3 scenarios: attempt-2-false-pass now correctly caught, genuine attempt-1 pass still passes, all-3-genuine-failures still fails) -- not committed as a repo test file since it exercises shell control flow, not Zig/Python source

Once fixed, re-run CI on a currently-open or new PR and confirm the retry loop's log output includes a real pass/fail summary line on every attempt, not just on timeout -- pending: will be observed on this fix's own PR CI run
resolution: Hardened .github/workflows/ci.yml's 'zig build test' retry loop: each attempt's combined stdout/stderr is now captured to a temp file via `tee` (exit code preserved through PIPESTATUS[0], compatible with the script's existing `set -uo pipefail`), and the loop's PASS condition now requires BOTH `status -eq 0` AND the absence of a 'failed command:' line in the captured output -- matching the exact marker Zig's build runner prints when any child Run step fails, independent of what the top-level process exit code ends up being. Verified via local bash simulation of all 3 relevant scenarios (see acceptance criteria) before committing, since the actual GH #22453-class contention that triggers the false-positive is not reliably reproducible on demand.
